WV-2026-HB5690.title: Supplemental appropriation, Adjutant General
WV-2026-HB5690.aiSummary: The bill adds $4,025,000 in state general revenue for the Adjutant General for fiscal year 2026. The money is for an Armory Board transfer from surplus funds. It affects the Adjutant General's office and its spending for that year.

WV-2026-HB5612.title: Relating to property valuations of properties located on the State Capitol Complex
WV-2026-HB5612.policyArea: Finance and Administration, Real and Personal Property
WV-2026-HB5612.aiSummary: The law changes how the state reports and tracks real property it owns or leases. It requires each agency to mark properties that are unused or mostly unused, and it removes the rule that the state must set a market value for that property. It affects state agencies and property on the State Capitol Complex.

WV-2026-HB4022.policyArea: Governor -- Bills Requested By, Human Services
WV-2026-HB4022.aiSummary: The law sets how Child Protective Services workers are assigned by county. Their numbers must be based on population, referrals, and average caseload, and cannot go below the bureau’s Jan. 1, 2023 level. The bureau must also send an annual report on any staffing changes and why they were made.

WV-2026-HB5582.aiSummary: The law extends a drug screening program for adults who apply for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families cash aid in West Virginia, through December 31, 2026, if federal approval is given. If a case worker finds reasonable suspicion, the person must take a drug test, and the human services department pays for the first test and the screening program. People who test positive may have to enter treatment and job skills programs, while children in the home keep their benefits and may have a protective payee named to receive them.

WV-2026-HB5528.aiSummary: This law lets certain public officials and some family members ask a government agency to remove or hide their home address, personal phone numbers, and related name details from public online records. If the agency does not do that after a written request, the person may go to court, and the agency may have to pay court costs and lawyer fees. The law still allows some sharing of this information for government work, law enforcement, legal process, property records, election work, and certain other listed uses.

WV-2026-HB5366.title: Relating to rules governing the practice of law

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 684)

Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB5366.aiSummary: The law sets rules for the practice of law in West Virginia, including lawyer ethics, judicial ethics, and discipline for attorneys. It keeps the West Virginia State Bar as part of the court system and requires lawyers in the state to be members in good standing. It also lets the court set fees for running the system, with yearly fees capped at $5 unless most lawyers agree to pay more, and makes certain assistance program records confidential if the court says so.

WV-2026-HB4538.title: Regarding fines in DOH work zones

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and title amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 637)
Unanimous consent to amend on 3rd reading

WV-2026-HB4538.aiSummary: The law changes fines for drivers who break traffic rules in road work zones. It lowers the top fines for failing to obey traffic instructions and for speeding or other traffic rule breaks in construction areas. Drivers who go 15 miles per hour or more over the posted limit in a work zone can also face up to 20 days in jail, or both a fine and jail time.

WV-2026-HB4484.title: To expand each county commission’s ability to sell or lease property.

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 378)

WV-2026-HB4484.aiSummary: County commissions in West Virginia would get broader power to sell or lease county real or personal property. The bill raises the small-item sale cutoff to $10,000, allows some sales by public auction, online auction, competitive bidding, or direct sale to private buyers under set price rules, and lets leases run up to 50 years after a public hearing. It also sets notice and posting rules for some sales and requires some property sold for public use to come back to the county if it is later sold again, unless the deed says otherwise.

WV-2026-HB4433.aiSummary: West Virginia’s law on human smuggling and trafficking would update crimes and penalties in those cases. It would add crimes for smuggling adults and minors, change some definitions, and allow civil asset forfeiture in some cases. It would also change rules on restitution, parole, fines, and aggravating circumstances, and create an exemption for medical, mental health, and legal services for an illegal alien. It was approved by the governor and became Chapter 191 in 2026.
